title: Stepdown + Circuit-Breaker Rollout UX: grooming and wireframe notes
body:
Purpose:
- Capture UX decisions and backlog tasks for implementing a stepdown / circuit-breaker pattern in the Rollouts Console. Focus areas: canary -> escalate -> stepdown (graceful scale-back) -> circuit-breaker auto-fallback paths.

High-level user story:
- As a platform engineer using Redwood Console, I want my rollout to automatically reduce traffic or cutover to a safe variant when latency/error thresholds are crossed, and to understand what happened via concise UI affordances so I can act quickly.

Design goals / constraints:
- Make automatic actions visible but reversible.
- Avoid surprising admins: show provenance (why triggered), exact metric snapshot, and a single-click undo where safe.
- Support both canary and A/B flows; circuit-breaker should be pluggable policy that can attach to any rollout.
- Keep primary console view usable at < 3 clicks for common recovery tasks.
- Integrate with existing tracing and cost breakdown panels.

Wireframe notes (frame-by-frame):
1) Rollout Summary card (compact)
   - States: Active | Paused | Auto-stepped-down | Circuit-tripped | Completed
   - Inline microcopy for auto actions: "Auto-stepdown applied: 60% -> 20% at 2024-11-12 14:22 GMT — triggered by latency > 500ms"
   - Primary CTA: "Open Incident" (opens side panel)

2) Incident / Event side panel (right drawer)
   - Header: status badge, timestamp, triggered-by metric, link to trace/trace id
   - Body: timeline of actions (canary started -> anomaly -> auto-stepdown -> fallback -> manual-override) with delta % traffic visual
   - Controls: "Revert stepdown" (one-click), "Escalate to full cutover" (confirm), "Mute alert for X mins"

3) Circuit-breaker policy editor (modal / inline composer)
   - Inputs: scope (route/model/version), window (N minutes), metric (p95 latency, error-rate), threshold, consecutive windows, action (throttle %, route to fallback variant, abort)
   - Preview: sample event timeline simulation given recent traffic (quick synthetic simulation using last 24h metrics)
   - Defaults: recommended by Optimize engine (e.g., latency p95 700ms for small models) with explainers

4) Canary traffic controls (timeline view)
   - Visual: stacked area showing traffic split over time with annotations where auto-actions occurred
   - Interaction: slider to scrub to historical time and buttons to apply manual changes at that moment (for replay/rollback)

Microcopy suggestions:
- Auto-stepdown banner: "Traffic reduced automatically due to elevated latency. Click for details or revert."
- Circuit-breaker tooltip: "An automated safety rule that reduces or redirects traffic when a health signal crosses configured thresholds."
- Undo affordance: "Revert (within 10 minutes)" with a small clock icon and reason auto-filled from event.

Backlog grooming (epics & candidate stories):
- EPIC RW-8290: Circuit-breaker rollout core integration
   - Story RW-8291: Data model for policy (store scope, metric, thresholds, actions) — AC: policy saved, editable, attached to rollout
   - Story RW-8292: UI: policy composer modal + validations + recommended presets — AC: composer renders, accepts presets, links to Optimize suggestions
   - Story RW-8293: Eventing: emit structured events when policy triggers (include sample payload) — AC: events visible in audit log and incident drawer
   - Story RW-8294: Undo / safe-reapply flow — AC: users can revert automated action within a configurable TTL
   - Story RW-8295: Timeline and visualization of traffic delta + annotation export — AC: PNG/SVG export for incident reports
   - Story RW-8296: Simulation backend for policy preview — AC: show predicted effect using last 24h sampled metrics
   - Story RW-8297: Integration tests with Dedicated/Dedicated-Fallback mode (ensure routing respects policy across infra)

Prioritization notes (MVP cut):
- MVP = basic policy attach + auto-stepdown (throttle %) + incident drawer with reason and undo. Visual timeline is low priority for MVP. Simulation is nice-to-have for Q2.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console can attach a circuit-breaker policy to a rollout and persist it.
- When metric crosses threshold in configured window, system performs configured action (throttle % or route to fallback) and console shows an "Auto-action" event in the side panel.
- Undo button re-applies prior configuration and emits an audit event.
- Event contains metric snapshot, timestamp, affected routes/models, and triggering rule id.

Open questions / risks:
- Who can configure automatic policies? (Assume rollout editors + org admins; need RBAC clarity)
- TTL for undo: 10m vs 1h? Shorter reduces blast radius of accidental reverts; longer supports ops work.
- How to present cost implications of fallback (e.g., fallback to smaller quantized model reduces cost but may change output quality)? Need inline cost delta estimate.
- Cross-region fallbacks: if primary region is unhealthy, circuit should support cross-region fallback. Operational complexity and data residency concerns.
- UX for chained policies (multiple policies targeting same route but different metrics) — need conflict resolution UI.

Telemetry / logging requirements (for SRE and audits):
- Emit structured event: {policy_id, rollout_id, action, metric_snapshot, previous_traffic_split, new_traffic_split, triggered_by, trace_id}  — ensure retention 90d
- Link incidents to tracing (trace id) for rapid RCA

Design alternatives considered and rejected:
- Auto-suggestion-only (no auto action) — rejected because fast-moving spikes require automated mitigation to meet SLOs, and manual ops would be too slow for many customers.
- Fully opaque auto-actions with only email notifications — rejected for user trust reasons. We prefer visible in-console events with reversible controls.

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: prototype composer modal in Figma and mark up component library tokens (due 2024-11-20)
- Marco: spike for simulation backend (metrics sample strategy) — estimate 2w (due 2024-11-26)
- Lina: draft RBAC proposal and docs for who can create/override policies (due 2024-11-22)
- Evan: coordinate with SRE for event schema and retention & add tickets to backlog (RW-8290 epic creation)

Notes to reviewers:
- Look specifically at undo UX and the recommended presets. Are the presets conservative enough for enterprise customers?
- Provide examples of existing customers who might need cross-region fallback (cc: solutions-engineering).
- Flag any regulatory constraints for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where cross-region routing is not allowed.

Quick links / references:
- Incident playbook draft: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/rollouts-incident-playbook
- Existing rollout timeline component: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/blob/main/src/components/Timeline.jsx
- Related Jira: RW-7122 (rollout timeline), RW-7901 (auto-fallback telemetry)

Random notes / brainstorm fragments (keep; very informal):
- "Could we show a tiny sparklines band on each route row to hint at rising latency before auto-action?"
- "When reverting, pre-fill a small blurb for changelog with 'reverted auto-stepdown triggered by p95 latency'"
- "Mobile view: collapse incident drawer into a single toast + 'Details' link"

End of doc.
